Q1: What should happen while `AUTOMATION_PATH_PLAN_AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED` is off (the default)?
Choices:
A) Flag off: skip automatic `/approved` for any plan that lists a protected automation path; ordinary plans are unchanged. Flag on: auto-approve only when every protected path in the plan has a trusted exact grant, and report the ones that don't. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Flag off: behave exactly as today, with no suppression. Flag on: do both the suppression and the grant check.
C) Flag off: behave exactly as today. Flag on: suppress automatic approval only, with no grant check.
**Note:** A is the literal reading of the issue and fails closed. B and C follow "keep the new behaviour off" and leave today's scope-block loop in place until the flag is turned on.
Q2: This issue's body has no `files_touched:` block, and every file the change needs is protected. How should the implementation get its grant?
Choices:
A) Before `/approved`, a trusted author (the GH_PAT login or an OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR) edits this issue body to add an exact `files_touched:` block. It lists `.github/workflows/plan.yml`, `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` and any other protected path the plan names; test files are not protected. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Go ahead without a grant and accept that implementation will be blocked again with `reason=no_allowlist`.
C) Change the scope to unprotected files only. **Note:** this cannot meet the request, because every file it targets is protected.
Q3: Which poller paths does "both poller recovery paths" cover?
Choices:
A) Only the two `auto_approve` stall-recovery actions: the managed one in `execute_stall_recovery_action` and the standalone one in `run_standalone_stall_recovery`. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Those two, plus the staged-support latch release, which also posts `/approved [auto-approved-by-plan]`.
C) Every place in the poller that posts `/approved`, including the unblock judge hand-offs.
Q4: When the flag is on and a plan lists protected paths without a grant, how should those paths be reported and denied?
Choices:
A) Skip automatic `/approved`, post one comment on the issue listing the ungranted paths, and leave the issue in `ai:awaiting-approval` for a person. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Skip automatic `/approved`, post the comment, and add `ai:scope-blocked`.
C) Skip automatic `/approved` and only log it (`AI_PHASE_GATE_V1 ... reason=automation_path_ungranted`), with no issue comment.
